article_content: In Hungary, a nationwide billboard campaign has recently been launched targeting European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. This campaign, which began this week, is seen as the start of an election effort and signifies growing friction between Hungary's conservative government and the European Union. Funded by the government, the billboards feature images of von der Leyen, who leads the EU executive and has been critical of some Hungarian policies, alongside Alex Soros, son of George Soros. George Soros is a Hungarian-American financier long portrayed by Hungary as a figure aiming to weaken its authority. The billboards carry the message: “Let's not dance to their tune." Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán has consistently adopted a confrontational approach to the EU. He has claimed that Brussels is trying to impose unwelcome policies on Hungary, even drawing parallels between EU membership and the Soviet era in Hungary. Conversely, the European Parliament stated last year that Hungary's government had evolved into “a hybrid regime of electoral autocracy,” suggesting it is no longer a full democracy. For over a decade, the European Commission has accused Orbán of systematically dismantling democratic institutions, seizing control of the media, and infringing upon minority rights since his rise to power in 2010. The billboard campaign against von der Leyen is part of a broader initiative to boost participation in Hungary's latest “national consultation.” This informal survey, distributed to all Hungarian adults, addresses contentious topics like migration, LGBTQ+ rights, and support for Ukraine. Peter Kreko, director of the Budapest-based think tank Political Capital, notes that this survey and ad campaign represent an “escalation of the government's anti-EU rhetoric” before upcoming European Parliament and local elections in June. Kreko added, "This national consultation is the most overtly anti-EU document released by the government to date. Their rhetoric towards Brussels has become highly irrational and increasingly counterproductive." One consequence of this strained relationship is the EU withholding billions in funding from Budapest due to concerns over rule of law and corruption. This financial setback is significant, especially after Hungary's year-long recession and ongoing high inflation. Initially, the government attempted reforms to access these funds, but after limited progress, this anti-EU campaign might suggest Orbán has abandoned these efforts, according to Dorka Takacsy, a research fellow at the Centre for Euro-Atlantic Integration and Democracy. Takacsy suggests, "Increasing the intensity of anti-EU messaging indicates that the Hungarian government may not intend to alter its approach to shared European issues. Despite the urgent need for EU funds in Hungary’s economy, the government might be willing to forgo this money rather than relinquish control." This isn’t the first instance of Hungary's government targeting EU leaders and the Soros family. A 2019 campaign similarly featured Jean-Claude Juncker and George Soros, which was criticized as antisemitic. Recently, observers have noticed a more aggressive anti-EU tone from Orbán, prompting discussions about a potential "Huxit." Kreko believes Orbán is conducting a “state-sponsored disinformation campaign” against the EU, with rhetoric even stronger than during the Brexit campaign. He speculates Orbán might aim to cultivate euroskeptic sentiment to leverage the threat of "Huxit" against the EU, even if he doesn't currently plan to leave. During a biannual congress of his governing Fidesz party, Orbán expressed a bleak outlook on the EU's future, stating he was “deeply convinced that we must say no to the Brussels model of Europe." He described the EU as "unsustainable" and "being destroyed and led to its ruins" by Brussels. However, EU spokesperson Eric Mamer dismissed these claims, expressing confidence in Hungarian voters to discern the truth behind Orbán's statements. Mamer said the national consultation was “completely untrue” and not in line with EU public opinion practices, and that von der Leyen was “completely unfazed” by the ads.

article_content: LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) -- Much attention has been given to Barack Obama's interest in "Team of Rivals," Doris Kearns Goodwin's acclaimed book on President Lincoln and his cabinet. Abraham Lincoln, pictured here at Antietam, dedicated considerable time to studying military history and strategy.  However, the president-elect might also benefit from reading "Tried by War: Abraham Lincoln as Commander in Chief" (Penguin), a new Lincoln book.  Authored by Pulitzer Prize-winning historian James M. McPherson, this work explores how Lincoln, an Illinois lawyer and self-taught military strategist, successfully led the nation through its bloodiest war.  Similar to Lincoln, Obama assumed office without personal military experience, yet became commander in chief during two ongoing wars. What lessons can Obama glean from Lincoln's example? CNN posed this question to McPherson, beginning with a discussion on how the 16th president evolved into what many consider the country's greatest commander in chief. The following is an edited transcript of the interview. CNN: Abraham Lincoln entered office in 1861 as the United States teetered on the brink of civil war. How did he rapidly prepare himself to make crucial military decisions? James M. McPherson: According to [Lincoln’s secretary] John Hay's diary, Lincoln devoted significant time to reading about military strategy, theory, and history to quickly educate himself.  Additionally, he sought knowledge by consulting numerous individuals with expertise in the subject. Lincoln, being a seasoned trial lawyer, was adept at cross-examination to extract information. This skill, asking questions and probing further, was another key method he used to learn. CNN: Lincoln quickly faced critical decisions, often encountering resistance or incompetence from field commanders. McPherson: Lincoln was likely surprised by the extent of his required involvement in almost daily strategic and command decisions.  The military commanders entrusted with these responsibilities frequently failed to meet the demands of the situation. Consequently, Lincoln felt compelled to intervene directly. Despite lacking prior military experience, Lincoln, from nearly his first day, had to make decisions with substantial military implications, often based on both purely military and political considerations inherent to his presidential role. CNN: In your book's introduction, you note Lincoln "proved to be a more hands-on commander in chief than any other president."  McPherson: Indeed, Lincoln exercised more direct control in shaping strategy and making command decisions compared to presidents like Woodrow Wilson in World War I and even Franklin D. Roosevelt in World War II.  For Lincoln, this hands-on approach was largely necessitated by circumstance rather than initial choice. CNN: Before Lincoln's presidency, the definition of commander in chief was unclear. McPherson: Lincoln essentially established the modern understanding of the commander in chief role. The Constitution simply states the president "shall be commander in chief of the army and navy of the United States and of the militia of the several states when called into federal service." It provides no further definition of presidential powers as commander in chief, and Lincoln had few relevant precedents in 1861. He essentially had to create them.  He asserted powers that, while not usurping Congressional authority over the military, were uniquely suited to the commander in chief. For example, he declared a blockade of the Confederate coast, an act of war.  He also expanded the Army and Navy without Congressional approval. He suspended habeas corpus, despite the Chief Justice arguing only Congress could do so. Lincoln maintained this was a necessary emergency function of the commander in chief, thereby setting another precedent. CNN: What lessons might President-elect Obama take from Lincoln as commander in chief? McPherson: Georges Clemenceau, the French prime minister during World War I, famously said, "War is too important to be left to the generals." Lincoln would certainly have agreed. Clemenceau meant that all aspects of warfare have political ramifications extending beyond the battlefield, impacting society as a whole.  Therefore, decisions cannot be based solely on military criteria. Lincoln grasped this deeply, and it’s a crucial consideration for Obama.  Obama likely understands that decisions about troop withdrawal from Iraq or troop increases in Afghanistan occur within a complex social, cultural, and political context, with far-reaching consequences. CNN: Lincoln effectively used his exceptional language skills during the Civil War. Can Obama learn from this? McPherson: Lincoln possessed the ability to clearly communicate ideas and policies to the general public, even complex ones. Obama shares this gift. CNN: Do you observe temperamental similarities between Obama and Lincoln, as some have suggested? McPherson: Yes, I do see similarities. While Lincoln occasionally lost his temper, he typically remained composed. This temperament—maintaining composure, controlling anger, and prioritizing rational thought over emotion—is a shared trait and a significant aspect of Lincoln's leadership. CNN: Finally, as a historian, are you pleased that Obama apparently values history? McPherson: Indeed, it's genuinely inspiring to have a president who reads history, understands history, and recognizes its importance. "Pleasure" is definitely the right word.
translated_content: LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) -- Mye har blitt gjort ut av Barack Obamas interesse for "Team of Rivals," Doris Kearns Goodwins anerkjente bok om president Lincoln og hans kabinett. Abraham Lincoln, avbildet her ved Antietam, viet betydelig tid til å studere militærhistorie og strategi. Likevel kan den påtroppende presidenten også ha nytte av å lese "Tried by War: Abraham Lincoln as Commander in Chief" (Penguin), en ny bok om Lincoln. Forfattet av den Pulitzer-prisvinnende historikeren James M. McPherson, utforsker dette verket hvordan Lincoln, en Illinois-advokat og selvlært militærstrateg, ledet nasjonen gjennom dens blodigste krig. I likhet med Lincoln tiltrådte Obama embetet uten personlig militær erfaring, men ble likevel øverstkommanderende under to pågående kriger. Hvilke lærdommer kan Obama trekke fra Lincolns eksempel? CNN stilte dette spørsmålet til McPherson, og startet med en diskusjon om hvordan den 16. presidenten utviklet seg til det mange anser som landets største øverstkommanderende. Det følgende er et redigert transkript av intervjuet. CNN: Abraham Lincoln tiltrådte embetet i 1861 mens USA balanserte på randen av borgerkrig. Hvordan forberedte han seg raskt for å ta avgjørende militære beslutninger? James M. McPherson: Ifølge [Lincolns sekretær] John Hays dagbok brukte Lincoln betydelig tid på å lese om militær strategi, teori og historie for raskt å utdanne seg selv. I tillegg søkte han kunnskap ved å konsultere en rekke personer med ekspertise på området. Lincoln, som var en erfaren rettssaksadvokat, var dyktig til å kryssforhøre for å trekke ut informasjon. Denne ferdigheten, å stille spørsmål og grave videre, var en annen viktig metode han brukte for å lære. CNN: Lincoln møtte raskt kritiske beslutninger, ofte med motstand eller inkompetanse fra befal i felten. McPherson: Lincoln ble sannsynligvis overrasket over omfanget av sin nødvendige involvering i nesten daglige strategiske og kommando-beslutninger. De militære befalene som ble betrodd disse ansvarsområdene, klarte ofte ikke å møte situasjonens krav. Derfor følte Lincoln seg tvunget til å gripe inn direkte. Til tross for manglende militær erfaring fra før, måtte Lincoln, nesten fra sin første dag, ta beslutninger med betydelige militære implikasjoner, ofte basert på både rent militære og politiske hensyn som var iboende i hans presidentrolle. CNN: I introduksjonen til boken din bemerker du at Lincoln "viste seg å være en mer praktisk øverstkommanderende enn noen annen president." McPherson: Ja, Lincoln utøvde mer direkte kontroll i utformingen av strategi og i å ta kommando-beslutninger sammenlignet med presidenter som Woodrow Wilson under første verdenskrig og til og med Franklin D. Roosevelt under andre verdenskrig. For Lincoln var denne praktiske tilnærmingen i stor grad nødvendiggjort av omstendighetene snarere enn et opprinnelig valg. CNN: Før Lincolns presidentskap var definisjonen av øverstkommanderende uklar. McPherson: Lincoln etablerte i hovedsak den moderne forståelsen av rollen som øverstkommanderende. Grunnloven sier bare at presidenten "skal være øverstkommanderende for hæren og marinen i USA og for militsen i de forskjellige statene når de blir kalt inn i føderal tjeneste." Den gir ingen ytterligere definisjon av presidentens makt som øverstkommanderende, og Lincoln hadde få relevante presedenser i 1861. Han måtte i hovedsak skape dem. Han hevdet maktbeføyelser som, selv om de ikke tilranet seg Kongressens autoritet over militæret, var unikt egnet for øverstkommanderende. For eksempel erklærte han en blokade av Konføderasjonens kystlinje, en krigshandling. Han utvidet også hæren og marinen uten Kongressens godkjennelse. Han suspenderte habeas corpus, til tross for at høyesterettsjustitiarius argumenterte for at bare Kongressen kunne gjøre det. Lincoln hevdet at dette var en nødvendig nødfunksjon for øverstkommanderende, og dermed satte han nok en presedens. CNN: Hvilke lærdommer kan president-elect Obama trekke fra Lincoln som øverstkommanderende? McPherson: Georges Clemenceau, den franske statsministeren under første verdenskrig, sa berømt: "Krig er for viktig til å overlates til generalene." Lincoln ville absolutt ha vært enig. Clemenceau mente at alle aspekter ved krigføring har politiske konsekvenser som strekker seg utover slagmarken og påvirker samfunnet som helhet. Derfor kan ikke beslutninger baseres utelukkende på militære kriterier. Lincoln forsto dette fullt ut, og det er en viktig vurdering for Obama. Obama forstår sannsynligvis at beslutninger om tilbaketrekning av tropper fra Irak eller økning av tropper i Afghanistan skjer i en kompleks sosial, kulturell og politisk kontekst, med vidtrekkende konsekvenser. CNN: Lincoln brukte effektivt sine eksepsjonelle språkkunnskaper under borgerkrigen. Kan Obama lære av dette? McPherson: Lincoln hadde evnen til å kommunisere ideer og politikk tydelig til allmennheten, selv komplekse ideer. Obama deler denne gaven. CNN: Observerer du temperamentmessige likheter mellom Obama og Lincoln, slik noen har antydet? McPherson: Ja, jeg ser likheter. Selv om Lincoln av og til mistet besinnelsen, forble han vanligvis rolig. Dette temperamentet – å opprettholde ro, kontrollere sinnet og prioritere rasjonell tankegang over følelser – er et fellestrekk og et betydelig aspekt ved Lincolns lederskap. CNN: Til slutt, som historiker, er du fornøyd med at Obama tilsynelatende verdsetter historie? McPherson: Ja, det er virkelig inspirerende å ha en president som leser historie, forstår historie og anerkjenner dens betydning. "Fornøyd" er definitivt det rette ordet.

article_content: The ongoing clash between people and the critically endangered Sumatran elephant in Indonesia has been a decades-long tragedy, with elephants suffering the most. Local villagers and farmers aren't killing elephants for sustenance; they are doing so to safeguard their homes and agricultural lands. This unfortunate situation, coupled with the shrinking of elephant habitats, has resulted in a staggering 80% decrease in their population since the 1930s, as reported by the IUCN Red List. In Riau Province, once home to the largest elephant population on the island in the 1980s, numbers plummeted from 1,342 in 1984 to a mere 201 by 2007. Land disputes are the primary driver of this conflict. Elephants naturally inhabit lowland areas, relatively flat landscapes below 300 meters in altitude. These very lands are also ideal for farming, leading to extensive deforestation as humans convert rainforests into agricultural fields. While a single small farm might seem insignificant, the cumulative effect, combined with massive forest clearing by large companies for palm oil and pulpwood plantations, leaves elephants with diminishing space. Despite being smaller than their African savanna relatives, Sumatran elephants are still massive creatures, the largest land mammals on Earth. Weighing up to 4,000 kg and standing up to 3.2 meters tall, they require vast areas to roam. Even protected forest areas of 250 km² are insufficient for a sustainable elephant population. Consequently, as their habitat dwindles, elephants are forced to venture into human-inhabited areas, including villages and farms, in search of food. One of their preferred foods is heart of palm, a delicacy also consumed by humans, found in the core of oil palm trees. To access it, an elephant must topple the tree, destroying a farmer's valuable crop. Oil palm is a highly profitable crop for Sumatran farmers. A single elephant can cause significant damage, flattening trees and trampling homes within minutes. A creature of this size is intimidating to anyone, especially when they forage at night. Villagers and farmers feel compelled to do whatever it takes to stop elephant destruction. Poisoning is the most prevalent method used by locals to kill elephants. They lace food with poison and leave it out, avoiding direct confrontation. Local communities don't desire to kill elephants; they believe they are left with no alternative. Some even express pride in the Sumatran elephant as a national symbol. While no villager believes killing one elephant will eradicate the species, the cumulative effect of these killings is, tragically, leading to population collapse. Organizations like the Sumatran Elephant Conservation Initiative (SECI) are working to change human-elephant interactions. SECI has introduced Riau province villagers and farmers to alternatives to lethal methods. They have developed scare guns that produce loud noises to deter elephants and alarm systems triggered by elephants crossing barriers. SECI has also assisted in installing electric fences bordering Bukit Tigapuluh National Park, a protected wildlife sanctuary. A key factor in the success of these programs is the education and cooperation of local residents. These non-lethal solutions utilize inexpensive, locally available materials, promoting quick adoption. Communities have established lookout posts and formed elephant watch groups to collectively scare away elephants using noise and fire. SECI's programs have effectively reduced elephant killings and are expanding. They now use radio tags to track elephants, enabling faster responses to prevent conflicts. These are small victories in specific Sumatran communities, but they are significant. If the killing of elephants can be stopped and deforestation controlled, the critically endangered Sumatran elephant population might have a chance at survival.
translated_content: Den pågående konflikten mellom mennesker og den kritisk truede sumatraelefanten i Indonesia har vært en tiår lang tragedie, der elefantene har lidd mest. Lokale landsbyboere og bønder dreper ikke elefanter for å spise dem; de gjør det for å beskytte hjemmene sine og jordbrukslandene. Denne uheldige situasjonen, kombinert med at elefantenes habitater krymper, har resultert i en svimlende 80 % nedgang i populasjonen siden 1930-tallet, ifølge IUCNs rødliste. I Riau-provinsen, som en gang var hjemmet til den største elefantpopulasjonen på øya på 1980-tallet, stupte antallet fra 1342 i 1984 til bare 201 i 2007. Landkonflikter er den primære årsaken til denne konflikten. Elefanter bor naturlig i lavlandsområder, relativt flate landskap under 300 meter over havet. Disse områdene er også ideelle for jordbruk, noe som fører til omfattende avskoging når mennesker omgjør regnskog til jordbruksarealer. Selv om en enkelt liten gård kan virke ubetydelig, fører den kumulative effekten, kombinert med massiv skogrydding av store selskaper for palmeolje- og tremasseplantasjer, til at elefantene får stadig mindre plass. Til tross for at de er mindre enn sine afrikanske savanneslektninger, er sumatraelefanter fortsatt massive skapninger, de største landpattedyrene på jorden. Med en vekt på opptil 4000 kg og en høyde på opptil 3,2 meter, trenger de store områder å streife rundt på. Selv vernede skogområder på 250 km² er utilstrekkelige for en bærekraftig elefantpopulasjon. Som en konsekvens av dette, når habitatene deres svinner hen, blir elefanter tvunget til å bevege seg inn i menneskebodde områder, inkludert landsbyer og gårder, på jakt etter mat. En av favorittmatene deres er palmehjerte, en delikatesse som også spises av mennesker, som finnes i kjernen av oljepalmetrær. For å få tak i det, må en elefant velte treet og ødelegge en bondes verdifulle avling. Oljepalme er en svært lønnsom avling for sumatrabønder. En enkelt elefant kan forårsake betydelig skade, jevne trær med jorden og trampe ned hus på få minutter. En skapning av denne størrelsen er skremmende for alle, spesielt når de leter etter mat om natten. Landsbyboere og bønder føler seg tvunget til å gjøre hva som helst for å stoppe elefantødeleggelser. Forgiftning er den vanligste metoden som lokalbefolkningen bruker for å drepe elefanter. De tilsetter gift i mat og legger den ut, og unngår direkte konfrontasjon. Lokalsamfunnene ønsker ikke å drepe elefanter; de mener de ikke har noe annet valg. Noen uttrykker til og med stolthet over sumatraelefanten som et nasjonalt symbol. Selv om ingen landsbyboer tror at å drepe én elefant vil utrydde arten, fører den kumulative effekten av disse drapene tragisk nok til populasjonskollaps. Organisasjoner som Sumatran Elephant Conservation Initiative (SECI) jobber for å endre samspillet mellom mennesker og elefanter. SECI har introdusert landsbyboere og bønder i Riau-provinsen for alternativer til dødelige metoder. De har utviklet skremmeskytevåpen som lager høye lyder for å skremme bort elefanter og alarmsystemer som utløses når elefanter krysser barrierer. SECI har også bidratt til å installere elektriske gjerder som grenser til Bukit Tigapuluh nasjonalpark, et beskyttet dyrelivsreservat. En nøkkelfaktor for suksessen til disse programmene er utdanning og samarbeid med lokalbefolkningen. Disse ikke-dødelige løsningene bruker rimelige, lokalt tilgjengelige materialer, noe som fremmer rask bruk. Lokalsamfunn har etablert utkikksposter og dannet elefantvaktgrupper for i fellesskap å skremme bort elefanter ved hjelp av støy og ild. SECIs programmer har effektivt redusert elefantdrap og utvides. De bruker nå radiosendere for å spore elefanter, noe som gir raskere respons for å forhindre konflikter. Dette er små seire i spesifikke sumatriske lokalsamfunn, men de er betydningsfulle. Hvis drapene på elefanter kan stoppes og avskogingen kontrolleres, kan den kritisk truede sumatraelefantpopulasjonen ha en sjanse til å overleve.

article_content: This month, 'Just Imagine' focused on how nature inspires solutions to humanity's greatest challenges. Scientists are gaining a greater understanding of biological processes and learning to manipulate them, including our DNA. Biotechnology advances are helping scientists find groundbreaking ways to create personalized medicine, detect illnesses, and eradicate disease. Futurist Ray Kurzweil believes this is just the beginning. He suggests that in the future, humans may be able to reverse aging, replace organs with new ones grown from their own DNA, and even genetically engineer unborn children. However, groups like the UK-based Human Genetics Alert worry that reprogramming our biochemistry could lead to dangerous consequences, including genetic discrimination and a redefinition of humanity. What do you think? To what extent should we alter our genetic makeup? Should there be limits, and how should they be determined? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

Futuristen Ray Kurzweil mener at dette bare er begynnelsen. Han antyder at mennesker i fremtiden kan være i stand til å reversere aldring, erstatte organer med nye som er dyrket fra deres eget DNA, og til og med genmodifisere ufødte barn. article_content: Cristiano Ronaldo scored four goals for the first time as Real Madrid retained top spot in Spain with a 6-1 thrashing of Racing Santander on Saturday. Defending champions Barcelona had briefly risen to the La Liga summit with a 2-0 victory at bottom club Zaragoza thanks to two goals from Lionel Messi, but Ronaldo outshone the world player of the year as Real ran riot. The Portugal forward increased his tally to 11 goals in 11 games this season -- eight of which have come in his last three league matches. Santander arrived in the Spanish capital just one point above the relegation zone, and attempted a defensive line-up with three center-backs which was repeatedly exposed in the first half. Gonzalo Higuain put Real Madrid ahead in the 10th minute with a composed finish after receiving Angel Di Maria's superb long pass for his fifth league goal this season. Then, five minutes later, he set up Ronaldo's first goal of the night with a low cross from the right. Ronaldo made it 3-0 in the 27th minute despite appearing to be in an offside position, sidefooting the ball home again, this time with his left foot, as Mesut Ozil mirrored Higuain's assist. Santander switched to a 4-4-2 formation at halftime, but it had no impact as Ronaldo completed his hat-trick two minutes after the break. He displayed excellent balance to turn and guide in a low cross from Di Maria which was slightly behind him. The world's most expensive player then made it 5-0 from the penalty spot in the 55th minute after Di Maria was brought down just inside the area, and Germany midfielder Ozil extended Real Madrid's lead from Xabi Alonso's throughball in the 63rd minute. Santander gained a small consolation 10 minutes later when midfielder Papa Diop's shot took a wicked deflection off teammate Markus Rosenberg's back, leaving Real Madrid captain Iker Casillas helpless in goal. The victory means Real Madrid have scored 16 goals in their last three league games, and Jose Mourinho's unbeaten team remain one point ahead of Barcelona. "We've been playing well for several games now, doing a good job overall and pressurizing our opponents as a whole team. Individual quality starts to shine through sooner when a team works well collectively," Mourinho told the Real Madrid website. "We have to start working on our game against Murcia [on Tuesday] as of now. Ozil, Carvalho and Xabi Alonso will have a three-day holiday. The rest will be called up for the match. [Karim] Benzema will be a starter, and so will Ronaldo." Messi increased his tally to four goals in a week after his two-goal performance in Barcelona's 2-0 Champions League win over Copenhagen. The Argentina forward put Barcelona ahead three minutes before halftime after being released by Spain striker David Villa's surging run on the counter-attack. Zaragoza, rooted at the bottom with just three draws from eight matches, then had midfielder Leonardo Ponzio sent off shortly after halftime following an incident involving Barcelona fullback Dani Alves. Barcelona capitalized in the 66th minute when Messi powerfully struck home the loose ball after the home defense failed to clear, while Villa later hit the outside of the post. Valencia could have joined Barcelona on 19 points, but lost 2-1 at home to Mallorca in the late match. The islanders led 2-0 before half an hour had been played as a much-changed home side suffered a second successive league defeat. Chori Castro scored both goals -- the first a sixth-minute penalty after striker Pierre Webo was clipped from behind, the second an opportunistic header after an earlier shot was blocked. Valencia, who drew 1-1 away to Scottish club Rangers in the Champions League in midweek, pulled one back from the spot in the 35th minute through Roberto Soldado but could not capitalize on an improved second-half showing. Third-placed Villarreal, also with 16 points, could move ahead of Barcelona on goal difference with a victory against Atletico Madrid on Sunday. In Saturday's only Italian Serie A match, Fiorentina moved up to 12th place with a 2-1 win at home to Bari -- a result that left both clubs among a group of six on eight points, eight behind leaders Lazio. Midfielder Marco Donadel opened the scoring in the 34th minute and Alberto Gilardino doubled the lead with eight minutes remaining before Alessandro Parisi's late consolation. Former Juventus coach Ciro Ferrara has been named the new coach of Italy's Under-21 team, replacing Pierluigi Casiraghi.

article_content: Hundreds of people ran naked into the sea as temperatures were low in an attempt to set a new world record for the biggest ever skinny dip. A crowd of over 200 people stripped off and ran into the sea at sunrise for The North East Skinny Dip in Druridge Bay, Northumberland, but failed to break the record. The event was organized to raise money for the mental health charity Mind, and organizers are confident they have raised thousands. Organizers believe the numbers fell short of breaking the record. People taking part said they also used it to celebrate their bodies as well as mark the autumn equinox. Organizer Jacqueline Higginson, 34, from Whitburn, said: 'I organized a skinny dip last year where we broke the world record. I don’t think there were enough people to break it [yesterday], but there were enough of us for it to be a lot of fun.' 'We chose Mind because I feel very close to mental health issues, both personally and as a paramedic, as I see them all around me.' 'And hopefully, I think we have raised thousands of pounds for Mind.' Last year, a skinny dip was held at Rhossili beach in Wales, where more than 400 people plunged naked into the sea and raised money for cancer charities and the National Trust. Ms. Higginson participated in that event, which inspired her to organize a similar event in the North East. The National Trust, which owns the section of beach used, gave permission for the event to take place.
translated_content: Hundrevis av mennesker løp nakne ut i sjøen da temperaturene var lave, i et forsøk på å sette ny verdensrekord for tidenes største nakenbading. En folkemengde på over 200 personer kledde av seg og løp ut i sjøen ved soloppgang for «The North East Skinny Dip» i Druridge Bay, Northumberland, men klarte ikke å slå rekorden. Arrangementet ble organisert for å samle inn penger til den psykiske helseorganisasjonen Mind, og arrangørene er sikre på at de har samlet inn tusenvis av kroner. Arrangørene mener at antall deltakere ikke var nok til å slå rekorden. Folk som deltok fortalte at de også brukte anledningen til å feire kroppene sine, samt markere høstjevndøgn. Arrangør Jacqueline Higginson, 34 år fra Whitburn, sa: «Jeg organiserte en nakenbading i fjor hvor vi slo verdensrekorden. Jeg tror ikke vi var nok folk til å slå den i går, men vi var mange nok til at det ble veldig morsomt.» «Vi valgte Mind fordi jeg føler et sterkt engasjement for psykisk helse, både personlig og i jobben min som ambulansearbeider, da jeg ser problemene rundt meg hele tiden.» «Og forhåpentligvis tror jeg at vi har samlet inn tusenvis av kroner til Mind.» I fjor ble det arrangert en nakenbading på Rhossili Beach i Wales, hvor over 400 personer kastet seg nakne i sjøen og samlet inn penger til kreftorganisasjoner og National Trust. Higginson deltok på det arrangementet, som inspirerte henne til å organisere et lignende arrangement i Nordøst-England. National Trust, som eier strandstrekningen som ble brukt, ga tillatelse til at arrangementet kunne gjennomføres.

article_content: KAMPALA, Uganda -- Can Idi Amin be rehabilitated? The question is animating some in this East African country two decades after the death of one of Africa's most infamous leaders. Amin, who took power by force in Uganda in 1971 and ruled until he was removed by armed groups of exiles in 1979, died in Saudi Arabia in 2003. His passing was barely acknowledged in Uganda, and some of Amin's supporters over the years have unsuccessfully lobbied for his remains to be returned home, underscoring his tainted legacy. Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni, whose rebel group was among those that ousted Amin with the help of Tanzanian troops, regularly dismisses Amin, and once even described him as “a primitive dictator.” There are no monuments to Amin in Kampala, the capital, where not even a street is named after him. But some Ugandans want to change that — not to emphasize Amin's tyrannical rule but to highlight any positive aspects of it, including what they say was his commitment to local industry as well as African solidarity. They have incited fierce debate over Amin's legacy at a time when many Ugandans are hungry for political change after nearly four decades of Museveni's presidency. Museveni, in power since 1986, has not said when he would retire. The effort to memorialize Amin is led by a former lawmaker from Amin's home region who asserts that Amin was defamed by international reporters who sometimes falsified stories about him. He says Amin deserves a more balanced verdict but he faces resistance from those who say Amin should just be forgotten. An Amin memorial lecture, the first of its kind, failed to happen as planned in September, because the event didn't receive approval from the education ministry. Hassan Kaps Fungaroo, the former lawmaker leading the effort, later wrote to education officials asking for support in the creation of an Idi Amin Memorial Institute. The matter reached Museveni, who characterized Amin's rule as “clearly illegal” and then rejected the idea of such an institute. “It is not acceptable to license an institute to promote or study the work of Idi Amin,” Museveni said in his response to the education ministry. “It is enough that forgiving Ugandans forgave the surviving colleagues of Idi Amin. Let that history be forgotten.” That verdict has sparked rebuttals from Ugandans who see some similarities between Amin and Museveni. Like Amin, Museveni took power by force and is heavily reliant on military authority to remain in power. And the president's critics cite rampant corruption, abuse of public resources, police brutality, and the shrinking space for perceived government opponents, arguing that Museveni has no moral authority to judge Amin. “Mr. Museveni thinks this country started with him and that he has performed miracles,” Joel Ssenyonyi, a lawmaker who is a spokesman for the opposition National Unity Platform party, told The Associated Press. “Our past leaders made mistakes, without a doubt, which Museveni likes to capitalize on, but he has done worse.” While Amin was a semi-illiterate leader who never pretended to be a democrat, Museveni has “captured all institutions” in the course of nearly four decades in power, Ssenyonyi said. Responding to criticism online of Museveni's directive, government spokesman Ofwono Opondo charged that a memorial to Amin may “glorify him but cannot undo his terrible deeds done in full view of many people, some still alive.” The suggested institute is an attempt to “whitewash” Amin's legacy, Opondo said. Amin's supporters and some academics point out that he was instrumental in acquiring or maintaining national assets at home and abroad, including a railway service, a national carrier, and multiple buildings housing Uganda's foreign missions. They say he also was committed to the nurturing of local talent in music and sports. But Amin's crimes are widely documented. A one-time heavyweight boxing champ and soldier in the British colonial army, Amin seized power in a coup d’état and then became the paranoid dictator whose government was accused of carrying out extrajudicial killings, forced disappearances and public executions. Between 100,000 and 500,000 people were killed during Amin's rule, according to Human Rights Watch. Some of Amin's actions drew harsh international attention upon Uganda. In 1972, he ordered the expulsion of tens of thousands of Asians who had controlled the country’s economy, sparking economic chaos. In the most notorious international incident of Amin's reign, a Palestinian group hijacked an Air France airliner to Uganda's Entebbe Airport in 1976 and kept its Israeli passengers as hostages. Israeli commandos flew to Entebbe under cover of darkness and rescued the captives, with Amin claiming he wanted to help negotiate a peaceful resolution despite some evidence he had been collaborating with the hijackers. Amin had almost no allies in the international community at the time he lost power. He fled to Libya, then Iraq and finally Saudi Arabia, where he was allowed to quietly settle down. Yet Museveni, a U.S. ally whose government regularly receives substantial foreign aid, insists that Uganda would be stronger economically if Amin had never been president. Some Ugandans frown at that, saying Museveni has had plenty of time to make his own mark. “The debate surrounding the proposed Amin institute shows how Museveni’s rule has polarized Ugandans,” said Gerald Bareebe, a Ugandan academic who is an assistant professor of politics at York University in Canada. “While many Ugandans abhor Amin, there are some who see similarities with Museveni’s rule, especially given the rising cases of forced disappearance, torture, extra-judicial killing and detention without trial under Museveni's regime.” ____ Follow AP’s Africa coverage at: https://apnews.com/hub/africa
translated_content: KAMPALA, Uganda -- Kan Idi Amin rehabiliteres? Spørsmålet engasjerer noen i dette østafrikanske landet to tiår etter døden til en av Afrikas mest beryktede ledere. Amin, som tok makten med makt i Uganda i 1971 og styrte til han ble fjernet av væpnede eksilgrupper i 1979, døde i Saudi-Arabia i 2003. Hans bortgang ble knapt anerkjent i Uganda, og noen av Amins støttespillere har gjennom årene uten hell lobbyert for at levningene hans skulle returneres hjem, noe som understreker hans beisk arv. Ugandas president Yoweri Museveni, hvis opprørsgruppe var blant dem som styrtet Amin med hjelp fra tanzanianske tropper, avviser jevnlig Amin, og har til og med beskrevet ham som «en primitiv diktator». Det finnes ingen monumenter over Amin i Kampala, hovedstaden, der ikke engang en gate er oppkalt etter ham. Men noen ugandere ønsker å endre på det – ikke for å understreke Amins tyranniske styre, men for å fremheve eventuelle positive sider ved det, inkludert det de sier var hans engasjement for lokal industri og afrikansk solidaritet. De har skapt en heftig debatt om Amins ettermæle i en tid da mange ugandere er sultne på politisk endring etter nesten fire tiår med Musevenis presidentskap. Museveni, som har vært ved makten siden 1986, har ikke sagt når han vil pensjonere seg. Forsøket på å minnes Amin ledes av en tidligere lovgiver fra Amins hjemregion som hevder at Amin ble baktalt av internasjonale journalister som noen ganger forfalsket historier om ham. Han sier Amin fortjener en mer balansert vurdering, men han møter motstand fra dem som sier at Amin bare bør glemmes. En minneforelesning om Amin, den første i sitt slag, ble ikke noe av som planlagt i september, fordi arrangementet ikke fikk godkjenning fra utdanningsdepartementet. Hassan Kaps Fungaroo, den tidligere lovgiveren som leder arbeidet, skrev senere til utdanningsansatte og ba om støtte til opprettelsen av et Idi Amin Memorial Institute. Saken nådde Museveni, som karakteriserte Amins styre som «klart ulovlig» og deretter avviste ideen om et slikt institutt. «Det er ikke akseptabelt å lisensiere et institutt for å fremme eller studere arbeidet til Idi Amin,» sa Museveni i sitt svar til utdanningsdepartementet. «Det er nok at tilgivende ugandere tilga de overlevende kollegene til Idi Amin. La den historien bli glemt.» Den uttalelsen har utløst reaksjoner fra ugandere som ser visse likheter mellom Amin og Museveni. Som Amin tok Museveni makten med makt og er sterkt avhengig av militær autoritet for å forbli ved makten. Og presidentens kritikere viser til utbredt korrupsjon, misbruk av offentlige ressurser, politibrutalitet og det krympende rommet for oppfattede regjeringsmotstandere, og argumenterer for at Museveni ikke har moralsk autoritet til å dømme Amin. «Mr. Museveni tror dette landet startet med ham og at han har utført mirakler,» sa Joel Ssenyonyi, en lovgiver som er talsmann for opposisjonspartiet National Unity Platform, til Associated Press. «Våre tidligere ledere gjorde utvilsomt feil, som Museveni liker å kapitalisere på, men han har gjort det verre.» Mens Amin var en halv-analfabetisk leder som aldri lot som om han var demokrat, har Museveni «fanget alle institusjoner» i løpet av nesten fire tiår ved makten, sa Ssenyonyi. Som svar på kritikk på nettet av Musevenis direktiv, anklaget regjeringstalsmann Ofwono Opondo at et minnesmerke over Amin kan «forherlige ham, men kan ikke omgjøre hans forferdelige gjerninger gjort for åpen scene for mange mennesker, noen fortsatt i live.» Det foreslåtte instituttet er et forsøk på å «hvitvaske» Amins ettermæle, sa Opondo. Amins støttespillere og noen akademikere påpeker at han var sentral i å anskaffe eller opprettholde nasjonale eiendeler i inn- og utland, inkludert en jernbanetjeneste, et nasjonalt flyselskap og flere bygninger som huser Ugandas utenriksstasjoner. De sier han også var opptatt av å fremme lokale talenter innen musikk og sport. Men Amins forbrytelser er bredt dokumentert. Amin, en tidligere tungvektsboksermester og soldat i den britiske kolonihæren, grep makten i et statskupp og ble deretter den paranoide diktatoren hvis regjering ble anklaget for å utføre utenrettslige drap, tvungne forsvinninger og offentlige henrettelser. Mellom 100 000 og 500 000 mennesker ble drept under Amins styre, ifølge Human Rights Watch. Noen av Amins handlinger vakte sterk internasjonal oppmerksomhet mot Uganda. I 1972 beordret han utvisning av titusenvis av asiater som hadde kontrollert landets økonomi, noe som utløste økonomisk kaos. I den mest beryktede internasjonale hendelsen i Amins regjeringstid, kapret en palestinsk gruppe et Air France-fly til Ugandas Entebbe flyplass i 1976 og holdt de israelske passasjerene som gisler. Israelske kommandosoldater fløy til Entebbe i ly av mørket og reddet fangene, mens Amin hevdet at han ønsket å bidra til å forhandle frem en fredelig løsning til tross for bevis på at han hadde samarbeidet med kaprerne. article_content: A NASA review, released on Wednesday, has concluded that there is no evidence to support claims that astronauts have flown aircraft or spacecraft while intoxicated with alcohol. The agency initiated the review following anecdotal reports suggesting that some astronauts had been permitted to fly while under the influence of alcohol. Bryan O'Connor, NASA's chief of Safety and Mission Assurance and a former astronaut, authored the report, which was subsequently published on NASA's website. O'Connor stated, 'Within the scope and limitations of this review, I was unable to verify any instance in which an astronaut spaceflight crewmember was impaired on launch day, or any case where a manager, flight surgeon, or fellow crewmember disregarded a recommendation that a crewmember should not fly on the Shuttle or Soyuz.' The review was commissioned in July after an independent panel, tasked by NASA, reported two alleged incidents where astronauts were purportedly so intoxicated that flight surgeons or fellow astronauts expressed concerns regarding flight safety. According to the panel, despite these concerns, the astronauts in question were still allowed to proceed with their flights. NASA convened the committee to investigate its medical and psychological screening procedures following the arrest of former astronaut Lisa Nowak in February. Nowak was arrested for the alleged attempted kidnapping related to another astronaut's romantic interest and has pleaded not guilty to the charges. The committee's July report indicated that 'Interviews with both flight surgeons and astronauts identified some episodes of heavy alcohol use by astronauts in the immediate preflight period, which has raised flight safety concerns.' The report further noted, 'Alcohol is readily available in crew quarters. Two specific instances were described where astronauts were so intoxicated prior to flight that flight surgeons and/or fellow astronauts raised concerns to local on-scene leadership about flight safety. However, these individuals were still permitted to fly.' Due to promises of anonymity to witnesses, the independent committee was hesitant to disclose sources to O'Connor. Consequently, O'Connor interviewed approximately 90 current and former astronauts, flight surgeons, nurses, technicians, managers, and crew quarters staff. He also examined records of safety hotline calls, submissions to the NASA Safety Reporting System, and NASA's close call and mishap reporting systems for any evidence of astronaut alcohol abuse. The report stated that he found no evidence of astronauts being inebriated. O'Connor noted that despite the availability of anonymous reporting, no such reports were filed. He further explained, 'The lack of privacy on launch day makes it nearly impossible to conceal alcohol use or alcohol-induced impairment.' 'Could a crewmember drink to the point of inebriation in his/her room the night before launch? Certainly,' O'Connor acknowledged, 'but from the time the crew awakens on launch morning until liftoff, they are constantly surrounded by other astronauts, managers, support crew, television cameramen, still photographers, crew quarters staff, and others.' The review recommends that NASA assign a flight surgeon to the suit-up room during astronauts' final launch preparations. This would 'allow more direct contact with the crewmembers on launch day and reduce the reliance on a suit tech (non-clinician) picking up any last-minute medical issue.'
translated_content: En NASA-gjennomgang, publisert onsdag, har konkludert med at det ikke finnes bevis for å støtte påstander om at astronauter har fløyet fly eller romfartøy mens de var alkoholpåvirket. Byrået startet gjennomgangen etter anekdotiske rapporter som antydet at noen astronauter hadde fått tillatelse til å fly mens de var påvirket av alkohol. Bryan O'Connor, NASAs sjef for sikkerhet og oppdragssikring og en tidligere astronaut, forfattet rapporten, som senere ble publisert på NASAs nettsted. O'Connor uttalte: 'Innenfor rammene og begrensningene av denne gjennomgangen, kunne jeg ikke bekrefte noen tilfeller der et astronaut-romfartsbesetningsmedlem var svekket på oppskytningsdagen, eller noen tilfeller der en leder, flylege eller medbesetningsmedlem ignorerte en anbefaling om at et besetningsmedlem ikke burde fly med romfergen eller Soyuz.' Gjennomgangen ble bestilt i juli etter at et uavhengig panel, oppnevnt av NASA, rapporterte om to påståtte hendelser der astronauter angivelig var så alkoholpåvirket at flyleger eller medastronauter uttrykte bekymring angående flysikkerheten. Ifølge panelet fikk de aktuelle astronautene likevel tillatelse til å fortsette med flygningene sine, til tross for disse bekymringene. NASA samlet komiteen for å undersøke sine medisinske og psykologiske screeningprosedyrer etter arrestasjonen av tidligere astronaut Lisa Nowak i februar. Nowak ble arrestert for påstått forsøk på kidnapping relatert til en annen astronauts romantiske interesse, og har erklært seg ikke skyldig i anklagene. Komiteens rapport fra juli indikerte at 'Intervjuer med både flyleger og astronauter identifiserte noen episoder med kraftig alkoholbruk av astronauter i den umiddelbare pre-flight perioden, noe som har reist bekymringer for flysikkerheten.' Rapporten bemerket videre: 'Alkohol er lett tilgjengelig i besetningskvarterene. To spesifikke tilfeller ble beskrevet der astronauter var så alkoholpåvirket før flygning at flyleger og/eller medastronauter uttrykte bekymring til lokalt lederskap på stedet om flysikkerheten. Disse personene fikk imidlertid fortsatt tillatelse til å fly.' På grunn av løfter om anonymitet til vitner, var det uavhengige panelet nølende med å utlevere kilder til O'Connor. Som følge av dette intervjuet O'Connor omtrent 90 nåværende og tidligere astronauter, flyleger, sykepleiere, teknikere, ledere og ansatte i besetningskvarterene. Han undersøkte også registre over sikkerhetshotline-anrop, innsendinger til NASAs sikkerhetsrapporteringssystem og NASAs systemer for rapportering av nestenulykker og uhell for å finne bevis på alkoholmisbruk blant astronauter. Rapporten slo fast at han ikke fant bevis på at astronauter var alkoholpåvirket. O'Connor bemerket at til tross for tilgjengeligheten av anonym rapportering, ble ingen slike rapporter innlevert. Han forklarte videre: 'Mangelen på privatliv på oppskytningsdagen gjør det nesten umulig å skjule alkoholbruk eller alkoholindusert svekkelse.' 'Kunne et besetningsmedlem drikke seg til alkoholpåvirkning på rommet sitt natten før oppskyting? Jada,' erkjente O'Connor, 'men fra det tidspunktet besetningen våkner på oppskytningsmorgenen og frem til oppskyting, er de konstant omgitt av andre astronauter, ledere, støttepersonell, TV-kameramenn, stillfotografer, ansatte i besetningskvarterene og andre.' Gjennomgangen anbefaler at NASA plasserer en flylege i suit-up-rommet under astronautenes siste forberedelser før oppskyting. Dette vil 'muliggjøre mer direkte kontakt med besetningsmedlemmene på oppskytningsdagen og redusere avhengigheten av at en dress-tekniker (ikke-kliniker) oppdager eventuelle medisinske problemer i siste liten.' article_content: CNN) -- Convicted Beltway sniper John Allen Muhammad is scheduled to be executed by lethal injection on November 10, a Virginia corrections official said Tuesday. 'Inmate John Muhammad was offered a choice in method of execution, and he declined,' Larry Traylor said. 'Under the code, if the inmate declines to choose, it defaults to lethal injection.' Muhammad was convicted of killing Dean Harold Meyers, one of several victims in a series of sniper-style shootings that terrorized the Washington area in October 2002. During a three-week period, Muhammad and his young protege, Lee Boyd Malvo, shot 13 people, killing 10 of them, police said. The two are also suspected in other shootings, including in Tacoma, Washington; Montgomery, Alabama; and elsewhere in the Washington metro area. Attorneys for Muhammad argued last week that he should be given clemency on the grounds that he has a severe mental illness that worsened while he served in the Persian Gulf War. Attorney Jonathan Sheldon said that he and other attorneys presented Virginia Gov. Tim Kaine's representatives with audio interviews with attorneys, mental health experts and witnesses rather than a written document. They said they plan to file an appeal with the U.S. Supreme Court on November 3. Kaine's office said that any information on the clemency request would come in the form of a news release at a later date. CNN's Mike M. Ahlers contributed to this report.

article_content: A wedding attendee, under the influence of alcohol, mistakenly entered a woman's hotel room and groped her as she slept. Despite this action, he avoided immediate imprisonment because the judge presiding over the case stated, 'you are not a sexual predator.' David Rawson, aged 25, committed this act after the victim opened her door at 4 am, believing it was her female roommate returning. Due to the darkness, she didn't recognize Rawson, a former soldier, and went back to bed. Subsequently, Rawson got into bed with the woman and began to grope her. Burnley Crown Court was informed that Rawson was 'out of his head' after consuming cocaine, beer, and wine at a wedding celebration held at the Oaks Hotel in Brierfield, Lancashire, a venue with 50 rooms. Prosecutor Mark Lamberty mentioned that both Rawson and the victim were guests at the wedding reception. As Rawson proceeded with the assault, the victim became aware of what was happening, pushed him away, and sought help from the reception area. Mr. Lamberty added that the woman returned to her room and instructed Rawson to leave, but he refused. She then dressed, left the room, and contacted the police. Following the incident, Rawson engaged in a physical altercation with his brother, which ended with Rawson grabbing his brother by the neck and pushing him against a wall. Others intervened to calm him down, and he began to cry. Rawson, employed at a carpet factory, was questioned and admitted to the fight with his brother. However, he initially denied entering the woman's room and the sexual assault, later admitting to sexual touching and two counts of assault by beating related to the May 31st event. Defense lawyer David Bruce described the case as 'quite unusual and sad,' noting Rawson had left military service the previous year. The incident occurred at the Oaks Hotel in Brierfield, Lancashire, where the woman was staying following a wedding reception. Mr. Bruce further stated that Rawson had recently broken up with his girlfriend and had been hospitalized for a suicide attempt. He added, 'He has very little memory of that evening. He was completely intoxicated, having consumed a mix of anti-depressants, drugs, and alcohol.' 'He sees this incident as occurring during a very dark period in his life. He cannot explain his actions and is deeply ashamed of what he did that night.' Rawson, from Bury, received a 14-month jail sentence, suspended for two years, along with 12 months of supervision and was placed on the Sex Offenders’ Register for 10 years. Judge Beverley Lunt told Rawson, 'I believe this is completely out of character for you because you were under the influence of a cocktail of alcohol and drugs. You are not a sexual predator or a sexual threat to society.' 'The root cause of this entire incident was drug and alcohol abuse.' Rawson, 25, was 'out of his head' after consuming cocaine, beer, and wine at the wedding celebration. Following the incident, Rawson was involved in a fight with his brother, leading to police intervention and his arrest.

article_content: A dispute has arisen involving Queen Elizabeth and Members of Parliament regarding the potential authorization of same-sex marriage ceremonies within Parliament's chapel. Lawmakers are advocating for St Mary Undercroft, the primary Christian worship site in the Palace of Westminster, to be available for gay weddings. This proposition, deemed contentious, is reportedly backed by John Bercow, the Speaker of the House of Commons. Sources indicate that Sir Christopher Geidt, the Queen's Private Secretary, is also being consulted about the possibility of permitting same-sex marriages at St Mary Undercroft. While the Church of England is exempt from legislation legalizing gay marriage, and thus prohibits same-sex weddings on its grounds, allowing such ceremonies in St Mary Undercroft could necessitate severing the chapel's ties with the Church, according to reports. St Mary Undercroft is a sought-after wedding location for MPs, having hosted the marriages of figures like William Hague. However, due to its status as a "Royal Peculiar" under the Queen's jurisdiction, this issue now involves both the Queen and Buckingham Palace. Emails seen by a newspaper suggest the involvement of Lt Gen David Leakey (Black Rod), a senior official in the House of Lords. Labour MP Chris Bryant has suggested transforming the chapel into a multi-faith venue to accommodate various religious denominations in conducting same-sex weddings within Parliament. Mr. Bryant, a former Anglican vicar, requested Equalities Minister Helen Grant to seek the Queen's permission to repurpose St Mary Undercroft for multi-faith use, facilitating same-sex weddings. Mrs. Grant expressed willingness to consider government assistance. Mr. Bryant has also approached Speaker Bercow for help in easing chapel restrictions. Bercow is reportedly seeking advice but is considered sympathetic to the idea. This situation potentially puts Bercow at odds with the Archbishop of Canterbury, Justin Welby, who is being briefed on the unfolding situation. Mr. Bryant has also reportedly engaged with other key figures in Parliament, Buckingham Palace, and the Church. Lt Gen Leakey is believed to oppose Mr. Bryant's proposals. Tory MP Gary Streeter has cautioned about significant opposition to converting the chapel into a multi-faith space, based on disclosed correspondence. article_content: A 62-year-old man from Brooklyn, Albert Tarrats, is set to be imprisoned after his stepdaughter's college application essay revealed a rape he committed over ten years ago. Tarrats sexually assaulted his then eight-year-old stepdaughter in 2003 while she was asleep. This appalling crime was brought to light when the victim, now 19, detailed the assault in an essay in 2012. After reading the essay, her mother promptly contacted law enforcement. Following his conviction on Thursday, Tarrats could receive a prison sentence of up to 25 years. The conviction took place at Brooklyn Criminal Court, where Albert Tarrats was found guilty on multiple charges, including rape and sexual assault. In her essay, the teenager wrote about the beginning of the rapes towards the end of her parents' marriage. She explained she was too scared to tell anyone until much later. Last week, she testified in court about the ongoing pain caused by his heartless actions. A juror informed the New York Daily News that she was very believable. The juror added that the passage of time since the assault made them believe she had no hidden agenda. The victim's mother divorced Tarrats in 2005 and relocated to Florida with her daughter. Jurors dismissed the defense's attempts to portray the allegations as either revenge for the failed marriage or a ploy to gain sympathy from college admissions. According to the New York Post, Tarrats' lawyer, Earnest Hammer, argued in his closing statement that the essay was simply an attempt to gain the college admissions committee's attention and convince them she was the best candidate. Hammer emphasized her grammatical errors and highlighted her rejection from the college. Another juror commented on how impactful this rejection must have been on her life. The jury convicted Tarrats on multiple counts, including rape and sexual assault. He displayed no emotion as the verdicts were announced in court. His sentencing is scheduled for June 30.

article_content: Tetsuya Kumakawa is widely regarded as not just Japan's greatest ballet dancer, but one of the world's best. His performances are known for their athletic grace, captivating audiences globally and expanding ballet's reach. Known affectionately as "Teddy," Kumakawa is celebrated for his incredible leaps and flawless technique. Building on his success at London's Royal Ballet, he established the K-Ballet company in 1998. Born in Sapporo, Japan, in 1972, Kumakawa was inspired to start ballet at age ten after watching his cousin Hironao perform. Ballet quickly became his passion, even alongside other interests like kendo, baseball, and drawing. From a young age, Kumakawa dreamed of seeing the world, a desire amplified by visiting international ballet instructors. A pivotal moment came with Swiss teacher Hans Meister, who encouraged Kumakawa to study at prestigious schools like the Royal Ballet School in London or the Canadian National Ballet School. At just 15, Kumakawa moved to London to attend the Royal Ballet School. In 1989, at age 16, he achieved significant recognition by winning both the Gold Medal and the Prince Takamado Prize at the Prix de Lausanne in Switzerland, particularly impressing with his performance from "Don Quixote." Turning professional in spring 1989, Kumakawa made history as the first Asian dancer in the Royal Ballet Company, debuting in a solo role in "Romeo and Juliet." His rapid ascent continued when he won the Classical Ballet Prize at the Eurovision Young Dancer competition in Paris in June. Kumakawa quickly rose through the Royal Ballet ranks, becoming a Soloist and delivering memorable performances, especially as the Bronze Idol in "La Bayadère." He was also chosen for a key role in Kenneth Macmillan's "The Prince and the Pagodas." By 1991, he was a First Soloist and by 1993, a Principal dancer, fostering a strong connection with his British fans and London. Kumakawa expressed his delight in being part of British culture. By 26, known as "Teddy" in the UK, he had performed a wide range of classical and modern roles with the Royal Ballet. In 1998, he embarked on a new venture, founding the K-Ballet in Tokyo, a move that caused considerable controversy, especially as he brought several Royal Ballet stars with him. Despite criticism from the British ballet scene, Kumakawa was hailed as a hero in Japan, taking on multiple roles within his new company. Under his leadership, K-Ballet thrived, boosting ballet's popularity in Japan. In 2004, he expanded his efforts by establishing the K-Ballet School. That same year, K-Ballet made history as the first Japanese ballet company to perform at the Metropolitan Opera House in New York. A knee injury in 2007 temporarily stopped his performing career, but he anticipated returning to the stage. Even while recovering, Kumakawa, a celebrity in Japan, continues to mentor the next generation of dancers.

Ballett ble raskt hans lidenskap, selv ved siden av andre interesser som kendo, baseball og tegning. article_content: On March 15, 2013, a distressing discovery was made near the training grounds of the Bolton Wanderers football club. The body of a newborn infant was found abandoned in Lostock, close to fields used by the club's academy in Ox Hey Lane.  Accompanying the baby was a note indicating a wish for an Islamic burial. A couple walking their dog in the afternoon stumbled upon the child, who was wrapped in clothing and plastic bags. The location was approximately a mile from Bolton Wanderers' Reebok Stadium. Police have launched a forensic investigation at the scene on Ox Hey Lane.  Authorities have cordoned off the area where the baby was found, near the academy training fields. At this point, details such as the baby's age, gender, and ethnicity remain unknown, as does whether the baby was born alive. Chief Inspector Carol Martin expressed the gravity of the situation, stating the police are focused on two main objectives: determining the time and cause of the baby's death and finding the parents. Chief Inspector Martin conveyed deep concern for the parents' well-being, especially the mother, who is likely in need of medical support. She directly appealed to the parents, or anyone with information, to contact the police, their GP, or a local hospital.  Support services are available to assist the parents during this difficult time. While the parents' ethnicity is not confirmed, the note requesting an Islamic burial has prompted police to engage with the Muslim community through the Bolton Council of Mosques and Friday prayers.  Investigators believe the answers lie within the local community and are asking residents to consider if they know anyone who may have hidden a pregnancy, recently given birth without a baby, or is showing signs of distress or physical discomfort. A post-mortem examination by the Home Office is scheduled for Monday. Super Int Steve Nibloe of Greater Manchester Police confirmed a significant police presence at the location and acknowledged the upsetting nature of the incident. He reassured the community that police are working diligently to find answers and urged anyone with information about the mother or any relevant details to contact them. Police confirmed the baby was found at 4:55 pm the previous day but have not yet released the baby’s sex.

Stedet var omtrent en kilometer fra Bolton Wanderers' Reebok Stadium. Politiet har startet en kriminalteknisk etterforskning på stedet i Ox Hey Lane. Myndighetene har sperret av området der babyen ble funnet, i nærheten av akademiets treningsfelt. På nåværende tidspunkt er detaljer som babyens alder, kjønn og etnisitet fortsatt ukjente, i likhet med om babyen ble født levende. Politimester Carol Martin uttrykte alvoret i situasjonen og sa at politiet er fokusert på to hovedmål: å fastslå tidspunktet og årsaken til babyens død, og å finne foreldrene. Politimester Martin uttrykte dyp bekymring for foreldrenes velvære, spesielt moren, som sannsynligvis trenger medisinsk hjelp. Selv om foreldrenes etnisitet ikke er bekreftet, har lappen som ba om en islamsk begravelse fått politiet til å engasjere seg med det muslimske miljøet gjennom Bolton Council of Mosques og fredagsbønner. Politiet bekreftet at babyen ble funnet klokken 16:55 dagen før, men har ennå ikke offentliggjort babyens kjønn.

article_content: Kathryn E Strachan, CEO of the award-winning B2B content marketing agency CopyHouse, highlights the transformative impact of AI on content marketing. While acknowledging AI’s rapid evolution, Strachan notes the confidence of creative professionals in their job security, attributing it to their adaptation through human-AI collaboration. This article explores the reasons and methods for leveraging AI tools to enhance content production and boost efficiency. AI’s Influence on Content Marketing AI is reshaping content marketing in two primary ways: content creation and content curation/optimization. Firstly, AI generates content directly. This process, now common, involves users providing prompts to generative AI platforms for text or image outputs. Major brands like Microsoft, Google, Adobe, and Salesforce are integrating these systems to enhance user productivity, recognizing the potential productivity gains. Secondly, AI aids in content curation and optimization. Platforms like Semrush and Google offer intelligent systems that identify and capitalize on content marketing opportunities. Data-driven insights can save time and improve campaign performance by reducing inefficiencies. Overall, AI enables marketers to produce more content, easily personalized and optimized for different channels. Effective Human-AI Collaboration Despite concerns about AI inaccuracies, its potential productivity benefits necessitate learning to work with, rather than against, AI. The exact nature of this collaboration will vary by organization. However, AI can be integrated throughout the content marketing workflow, starting with idea generation. AI can efficiently access market research, overcoming analysis paralysis and providing current insights into customer needs. AI tools can then create initial drafts for human editing and refinement, accelerating content production and meeting deadlines. These tools can also assist with spell-checking, tone guidance, imagery standards, and keyword density. Benefits of Integrating AI and Human Skills The advantages of AI in content marketing are significant, as previously mentioned. Crucially, the role of human professionals in these processes must be emphasized. AI is not yet capable of fully replacing human content marketers, making human oversight essential. The primary benefit of combining AI and human expertise is empowering marketers to become content orchestrators and brand leaders. By reducing content production workload, marketers can focus on strategic roles, ensuring content quality, consistency, accuracy, and brand resonance. AI also optimizes marketing budgets and amplifies brand achievements. The future of content marketing is promising, offering marketers unprecedented productivity, real-time feedback, and optimization suggestions. Moving Forward with AI It is important to note that AI tools should enhance process efficiency and reliability. Prompt variations can lead to output inconsistencies, and neglecting brand standards can compromise content quality compared to traditional methods. Awareness of AI pitfalls and mitigation strategies is crucial, starting with prompt engineering (refer to McKinsey’s guide). Experimentation with prompt detail, clarity, and model temperature refines AI outputs. Embedding brand guidelines throughout content processes is also vital, similar to training new staff. However, errors can still occur, necessitating thorough output reviews, especially in regulated sectors with strict advertising standards, where source accuracy and nuance are paramount. Key Takeaways for the Future of Content Marketing AI is revolutionizing content marketing, mirroring its impact across industries. Despite job loss predictions, human-AI collaboration offers a viable path for creative professionals. In this evolving landscape, AI and human expertise are complementary, not mutually exclusive. Professionals who embrace this perspective and develop necessary skills will thrive, driving marketing and brand awareness success. Training and experimentation are crucial, particularly as generative AI platforms develop. Regular prompt engineering and review sessions are vital to prevent public dissemination of inaccurate information. Forbes Agency Council is an invitation-only community for agency executives.
